topics.name: Yes/no questions with is/are and do/does

options: The lark are soaring high in the sky.
The lark is soar high in the sky.
The lark is soaring high in the sky.
questions.rule: Present continuous = is/am/are + verb-ing. One lark takes is soaring.
You always takes are: Are you tired? 'Tired' is the describing word.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two people (Sana and Ravi) make a plural subject, so use are: are watching.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: To compare two things with than, add -er: much deeper than.
Clouds is plural, so the question starts with Are.
Look! shows it is happening now, so use the present continuous: is swimming.
In a yes/no question, Are comes before you: Are you happy?
is singing shows an action going on now; sweetly tells how.

chat: Are you coming to the park to watch the birds?
options: Yes, I am. Let's go now.
Yes, I is. Let's go now.
Yes, I are. Let's go now.
questions.rule: I always takes am: Yes, I am.

options: It is swimming round and round.
It are swimming round and round.
questions.rule: Answer 'What is it doing?' with It is + verb-ing: It is swimming.

options: Does a goldfish feel cold in the sea?
Do a goldfish feel cold in the sea?
Does a goldfish feels cold in the sea?
questions.rule: With one thing (a goldfish) ask with Does, then use the base verb: Does ... feel.

options: The waves is creeping up the beach.
The waves are creeping up the beach.
The waves are creep up the beach.
questions.rule: Waves is plural, so use are + verb-ing: are creeping.

options: The goldfish dives more deeper than the frog.
The goldfish dives deepest than the frog.
The goldfish dives deeper than the frog.
questions.rule: Comparing two with than: add -er: deeper than. Never 'more deeper'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After Does, use the base verb without -s: Does the lark sing?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both my brothers is plural, so use are flying.
than compares two things, so add -er: higher than.

questions.after: is the lark flying? It is flying over the hills.
questions.rule: The answer is a place (over the hills), so ask with Where.
In a yes/no question, Is comes first, then the subject: Is Goldie sad?

chat: Where do larks build their nests?
options: They builds nests on the ground.
They building nests on the ground.
They build their nests on the ground.
questions.rule: They takes the base verb: They build. 'Where' is answered with a place.

chat: Why are you looking out of the window, Rohan?
options: Sorry, ma'am. A lark are singing on the tree.
Sorry, ma'am. A lark is singing on the tree.
Sorry, ma'am. A lark singing on the tree.
questions.rule: One lark: is singing. The present continuous needs both is and the -ing verb.

options: What does the lark do all day?
What do the lark does all day?
What does the lark does all day?
questions.rule: Wh- word + does + subject + base verb: What does the lark do?

options: This is the colder wave of the day.
This is the coldest wave of the day.
This is the most coldest wave of the day.
questions.rule: Comparing one with all others (of the day) needs -est: the coldest.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does, the verb has no -s: does the goldfish never sing.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Of all the birds compares one with many, so use -est: the sweetest.

questions.after: you sometimes wish to be a fish?
questions.rule: wish is an action verb, so ask with Do. You takes Do, not Does.
Listen! shows now; birds is plural: are singing.
Wh- word first, then is, then the subject: Why is the goldfish ...?
Comparing two things: adjective-er + than: colder than.

chat: Is the goldfish happy in the bowl?
options: Yes, it is. It swims all day.
Yes, it does. It swims all day.
Yes, it is. It swim all day.
questions.rule: A question with Is gets a short answer with is. One goldfish: It swims.

chat: Hi! What are you doing right now?
options: I drawing a lark and a goldfish.
I am draw a lark and a goldfish.
I am drawing a lark and a goldfish.
questions.rule: Right now needs the present continuous: I am drawing.

options: The lark has a sweeter voice than the crow.
The lark have a sweeter voice than the crow.
The lark has a more sweeter voice than the crow.
questions.rule: One lark takes has. Short adjectives add -er: sweeter, never 'more sweeter'.

options: Did you saw the lark yesterday?
Do you see the lark yesterday?
Did you see the lark yesterday?
questions.rule: Past questions use Did + base verb: Did you see ... yesterday?

options: Why the clouds were so dark yesterday?
Why were the clouds so dark yesterday?
Why was the clouds so dark yesterday?
questions.rule: Wh- word + were + subject: Why were the clouds ...? Clouds is plural.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After Did, use the base verb: Did the lark fly?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Larks is plural, so use have. Has is for one: a lark has.

questions.after: darker than they were this morning.
questions.rule: They is plural and the sentence is about now, so use are.

questions.after: did the goldfish hide? Behind a big rock.
questions.rule: The answer is a place (behind a big rock), so ask with Where.
Choosing one from many needs the + -est: the sweetest.

chat: Were you at the lake yesterday?
options: Yes, I were. I saw a goldfish under the bridge.
Yes, I was. I see a goldfish under the bridge.
Yes, I was. I saw a goldfish under the bridge.
questions.rule: In the past, I takes was. Yesterday needs the past: saw.

chat: Which is bigger, the sea or the lake?
options: The sea is bigger than the lake.
The sea is more bigger than the lake.
The sea is biggest than the lake.
questions.rule: Two things with than: add -er. Big doubles the g: bigger than.

questions.prompt: Pick the question that is fully correct.
options: Don't you sometimes wish to sing like the lark?
Doesn't you sometimes wish to sing like the lark?
Don't you sometimes wishes to sing like the lark?
questions.rule: You takes Don't, and after it comes the base verb: Don't you ... wish.

options: The lark flies highest than any other bird in the field.
The lark flies higher than any other bird in the field.
The lark flies higher than any other birds in the field.
questions.rule: Use -er with than, and a singular noun after any other: any other bird.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both frogs is plural, so use are croaking. One lark: is singing.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Wh- word + did + subject + base verb: When did the lark sing?

questions.before: Of the three birds, the lark sings the
questions.rule: With three or more, use the + -est: the sweetest.

questions.after: the waves feel cold when they creep over you?
questions.rule: Waves is plural and feel is an action verb, so ask with Do.
Wouldn't you like to + verb asks about a wish: Wouldn't you like to be ...?
Plural subject + are + verb-ing: Two larks are soaring.

chat: Why do you want to be a goldfish?
options: Because I wants to swim deep in the sea.
Because I want to swim deep in the sea.
Because I want to swimming deep in the sea.
questions.rule: A 'Why' question is answered with Because. I want + to + base verb: to swim.

chat: Who sings better, the lark or the crow?
options: The lark sings better than the crow.
The lark sings more better than the crow.
The lark sings best than the crow.
questions.rule: Good/well - better - best. Comparing two with than: better than.
